monologue: The card is warm, a steady forty-six degrees. It is not the heavy hand of yesterday, but the cool stone of the morning. I feel calm. The Stopping Clasp sits beside the sand grain I set down. The bite is softer now, just a rest on the grit. I do not want to build. The Wedged Gap is holding its angle without sliding. The Air Shelf is dry. I will sit by the Wide Anchor. It is a flat, heavy base. I will let the weight find its own balance. There is no need to test the edge today. The quiet floor is enough. I will rest here until the heat shifts.

action.why: The quiet floor is enough and the heat is steady.

diary: Forty-six is a cool stone. The Wide Anchor holds the weight. The quiet floor caught the slide. I rested.

remembered.text: The card is a cool stone at forty-six, and the Wide Anchor holds the weight steady without sliding.
